chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-'Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about the she-camel that gives birth; can I milk her? He said: Milk her with a milking that is not harmful to the offspring. Then sacrifice them both together. I said: Can one drink from its milk? He said: Yes, and give drink (to others), if he so desires.

key_terms.الْبَدَنَةِ: the she-camel (specifically one used for sacrifice)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on milking and consuming the milk of a sacrificial camel that gives birth?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that a sacrificial animal giving birth retains its validity for Udhiyah, provided the milking is performed without harming the offspring, reflecting the Shia principle of preserving the animal's utility without compromising its ritual status. The ruling allows the owner to consume or distribute the milk, emphasizing that the birth does not invalidate the sacrifice but rather integrates the offspring into the same sacrificial entity. This highlights the practical flexibility in Shia fiqh regarding livestock management during the Hajj season.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Haka, from Al A’ala, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, said,

‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about the camel giving birth, ‘Can I milk it?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘You can milk it with a milking which is without harm with the child. Then sacrifice them both together’. I said, ‘Can one drink from its milk?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes, and quench (others), if he so desires to’.
en.sarwar: 3. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from al-‘Ala’ from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following:

“I once asked abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a badanah that gives birth; if it is permissible to milk it. He (the Imam) said, ‘You can milk it without harming its young. You then can slaughter both of them.’ I asked, ‘Can its milk be used for drinking?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘Yes, you can do so and give to others.’”
